correctness.rationale: Finite irreducible phase generator has invariant π_i proportional to reciprocal site speed, normalized by n+a. A bounded Poisson corrector gives the independent quadratic-variation identity. Exact differentiation and subtraction from the homogeneous baseline give two quadratics with discriminants 4(y-1)(y-4) and n²(y-1)(y-5). Hyperbolic monotonicity ensures 1<y<n with unique bias thresholds. An independent rational Poisson-solver script passed 40 exact checks. n≥3, p>q>0 and a>-1 cover all stated cases; no numerical extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: Full-text inspection of Derrida 1983 establishes a general periodic-walk diffusion law, which directly yields the specialized rational D and therefore is credited as prior. The new assessed mathematical object is the simultaneous sharp all-n bias/stage classification: double turning point becomes possible first at five stages, strict enhancement above the uniform baseline first at six, with unique drive thresholds and explicit intervals. The 2018 motor model demonstrates diffusion enhancement via finite stepping duration in a continuous potential-switching ratchet and does not state this site-speed-defect classification. Closest retrieved published results concerned spectral underdamping for one defective four-cycle and frequency-domain shot-noise plateaux for sequential cycles, rather than unwrapped diffusion noise as the site slowness varies. Residual risk is that the sharp classification has been derived implicitly or separately from the known general formula.

value.rationale: The site-speed defect is a physically natural isolated kinetic bottleneck. Complete exact phase diagrams identify the first possible size at which slowing causes nonmonotone diffusion (five stages), and the strictly stronger size necessary for a slower yet more dispersive motor (six stages). The monotone drift-vs-nonmonotone noise separation supplies a design-relevant structural comparison not conveyed by the known general diffusion formula alone.
